events.text: Second Circuit (summarizing trial evidence) stated that from 2009 through 2011 Ulbricht worked to get Silk Road up and running with programming help from others, including Richard Bates.

cites.quote: From 2009 through 2011, Ulbricht worked to get the site up and running, relying on computer programming assistance from others, including his friend Richard Bates.

events.notes: Range end 2011. Appellant brief (Br. 16) says Bates testified to helping in late 2010 and 2011.

events.text: Email text recovered from defendant's laptop, dated Sept 15, 2009 and attributed to 'Ross Ulbricht', asked about Tor hidden services and building an untraceable online storefront.
events.actors: FBI computer scientist Thomas Kiernan; Ross Ulbricht

cites.quote: On Sep. 15, 2009, at 17:01, Ross Ulbricht wrote,

events.notes: Kiernan Tr. 991:16-19 reads 'online storefront that couldn't be traced back to me (Tor hidden services?)'.

events.text: Trial evidence (journal entry on laptop) indicated Ulbricht began growing hallucinogenic mushrooms in 2010 to sell on the site to attract users.

cites.quote: in 2010 Ulbricht began to grow hallucinogenic mushrooms to sell on the site “for cheap to get people interested.”
I was calling it Underground Brokers, but eventually settled on Silk Road.
I was calling it Underground brokers but eventually settled on Silk Road. ... I finally decided that I would produce mushrooms

events.notes: Characterization of journal entry as described by 2d Cir. File last modified 2/27/2011 per metadata (Tr. 898:13). Journal first read through Kiernan on Jan. 21 (not in this file set). Alford tied it to a July 6, 2010 Craigslist email about renting a Bastrop country home (GX 314, Tr. 1277:23-25) and to July-Aug. 2010 "SR accounting" lab expenses matched to Gmail receipts (GX 250, 315-A, 315-B; Tr. 1278:6-1281:5). The government summation quoted the same passage (Doc 218, Tr. 2130:14-2131:3).

events.text: Testimony of SA Gary Alford: an email in Ulbricht's Gmail account dated September 24, 2010 asked a hosting company whether it was possible to set up a Tor hidden service on its servers.

cites.quote: On September 24, 2010 at 12:36 a.m. Ross Ulbricht wrote "Hi, is it possible to set up a tor hidden service on your servers?"

events.notes: The reply came from someone at roothosts.com (Tr. 1291:17-18).

events.text: Testimony of Richard Bates: a Google chat dated October 25, 2010 showed Ulbricht asking Bates for help with a Perl programming problem; Bates said such requests were "very frequent" in late 2010, before he knew of Silk Road.

cites.quote: This was October 25, 2010. ... log() is included in Math::Trig in perl, but my admin won't include the module

events.notes: GX 1000. Bates testified under a non-prosecution agreement. Doc 208 is the docketed "corrected" 1/22/2015 transcript; original Doc 206 has same text at pp.92-93, Tr. 1122:12-1123:23.

events.text: Government first learned of Silk Road and began investigating it in 2011 after international drug packages were intercepted at Chicago O'Hare airport.

cites.quote: The government first learned of Silk Road and began investigating it in 2011 after international packages containing drugs were intercepted at Chicago’s O’Hare airport.

events.notes: Appellant brief (p.31, Br. 14) says HSI Chicago SA Jared Der-Yeghiayan initiated the investigation based on intercepted mail packages.

events.text: Second Circuit stated that after Ulbricht created Silk Road in 2011, the USAOs for the District of Maryland and the Southern District of New York both investigated it; in 2012-2013 agents investigated Ulbricht, Anand Athavale and Mark Karpeles as possible DPRs.
events.actors: USAO-D. Md.; USAO-SDNY; Ulbricht; Athavale; Karpeles

cites.quote: After Ulbricht created Silk Road in 2011, the site attracted the interest of at least two separate divisions of the Department of Justice

events.notes: Range end 2013. Maryland office abandoned the Athavale/Karpeles theories; New York office identified Ulbricht.

events.text: Per the PSR as cited by the Second Circuit, Silk Road customers transacted approximately $183 million in illegal drugs from 2011 through 2013.

cites.quote: from 2011 through 2013, Silk Road customers transacted in approximately $183 million worth of illegal drugs.

events.notes: Range end 2013. Same figure at App. 6a ("According to the government").

events.text: Indictment alleged the narcotics-trafficking conspiracy (Silk Road operation) ran from in or about January 2011 through October 2013.

cites.quote: Count One charges that, from in or about January 2011 up to and including October 2013, the defendant engaged in a narcotics trafficking conspiracy.

events.notes: Complaint period was January 2011 to September 2013 (Gov. MTD opp., ECF 26 p.8). Appellant brief (Br. 8) uses Jan 2011–Oct 2013.

events.text: Testimony of SA Gary Alford: user "Altoid" registered on shroomery.org on January 27, 2011 and posted that day pointing readers to SilkRoad420.wordpress.com; the shroomery registration email went to RossUlbricht@gmail.com.

cites.quote: shroomery message board account has been created. Date is 1/27/2011, 6:22 p.m.

events.notes: GX 304, 305, 308-A. Shroomery post date (January 27, 2011) at Tr. 1261:25-1262:1; registration and post same day at Tr. 1263:4-10.

events.text: Testimony of SA Gary Alford: a January 29, 2011 bitcointalk.org post by "Altoid" (preserved as a quote in another user's reply) asked "Has anyone seen Silk Road yet?" and described it as an anonymous Amazon.com using bitcoin and Tor.

cites.quote: Has anyone seen Silk Road yet? It's kind of like an anonymous Amazon.com.

events.notes: Alford found it by date-restricted Google searches before Jan. 31, 2011 "because all information was that Silk Road had begun in February of 2011" (Tr. 1255:1-3). The original Altoid post was no longer on the forum; Alford tested that quotes survive deletion (Tr. 1264:20-1266:13).

events.text: Government stated the clearnet site "silkroadmarket.org" (instructions for reaching Silk Road on Tor) was hosted on a server controlled by Mark Karpeles's company from February 2011 to February 2012; later traced to a Kalyhost customer identified as Ulbricht (alias "Richard Page").
events.actors: Mark Karpeles; Ulbricht; SA Jared Der-Yeghiayan (HSI)

cites.quote: from February 2011 to February 2012, the website “silkroadmarket.org” was hosted on a server controlled by Mr. Karpeles.

events.notes: Range end 2012-02. Government letter brief of 2015-01-19 (ECF 154). Ex. B (154.2) is a 3/18/2011 email from staff@silkroadmarket.org to support@autovps.net.

events.text: By stipulation, an archive.org capture showed SilkRoad420.wordpress.com as it appeared on February 4, 2011, giving instructions for reaching the Silk Road Tor hidden service and listing offerings including marijuana, shrooms and MDMA.

cites.quote: as it appeared on February 4, 2011 when the web page was archived

events.notes: GX 303. Text quoted at Tr. 1260:15-1261:3.

events.text: Testimony of Brian Shaw: Silk Road's transaction database covered February 6, 2011 through October 2, 2013, with 1,530,252 transactions worth 9,912,070.05 bitcoins (about $213.9 million at recorded values) and commissions of 642,455.36 bitcoins (about $13.2 million).

cites.quote: it covered February 6, 2011 through October 2, 2013, so the entirety of what was in the database.

events.notes: Range end 2013-10-02. Totals at Tr. 1926:1-7. The earliest transaction is February 6, 2011, consistent with the government's "February of 2011" start (Doc 210, Tr. 1255:1-3); the defense pointed to "June 18, 2011" as the start of the site's "current form" (Doc 214, Tr. 1406:24-1407:1).

events.text: Testimony of Brian Shaw: of categorized Silk Road sales, about $182 million were drugs and pharmaceuticals and about $8.5 million were other items; fake-ID listings accounted for 3,642 sales worth $699,053.

cites.quote: So the drugs -- the total drug sales based on this analysis was approximately $182 million, correct?

events.notes: Range end 2013-10-02. GX 940A, 940B; fake-ID figures at Tr. 1934:5-8. About $22 million in uncategorized ("null") sales were excluded (Tr. 1925:21-23).

events.text: WHOIS record showed silkroadmarket.org registered Feb 28, 2011 (registrant 'Richard Page'), expiring Feb 28, 2012.
events.actors: HSI SA Jared Der-Yeghiayan; Joshua Dratel

cites.quote: It's registered on February 28, 2011, right?

events.notes: CONFLICT: draft affidavit described registration as March 1, 2011 (200 Tr. 500:10); WHOIS history shows 'old registrar information, March 12, 2011' (204 Tr. 1006:8).

events.text: Testimony of Richard Bates: in a February 28, 2011 Google chat he forbade Ulbricht from mentioning his "secret project"; soon after, given an ultimatum, Ulbricht told Bates he was building a drug-sales website and showed him the Silk Road homepage (Bates placed this in late Feb/early March 2011).

cites.quote: I'm officially forbidding you from mentioning your secret project to me again unless you are going to reveal it. ... he showed me the Silk Road homepage for the first time.

events.notes: GX 1001. Bates elsewhere said he learned "late February/early March of 2011" (Tr. 1104:4-5). Doc 208 is the docketed "corrected" 1/22/2015 transcript; original Doc 206 has same text at pp.95-96, Tr. 1125:4-1126:4.

events.text: Der-Yeghiayan's May 29, 2013 draft affidavit stated Silk Road was launched in March 2011.

cites.quote: And you said that Silk Road had been launched in March of 2011, right? A. Correct.

events.notes: Laptop net-worth spreadsheet notes 'launch sr' at April 2011 (204 Tr. 958:6-7).

events.text: Testimony of Richard Bates: around March 2011, while drinking at a bar, Ulbricht offered him an administrator role on Silk Road and complained that the administrative workload was becoming too much and he would need to hire admins.

cites.quote: Ross came up to me and said something akin to, Hey, do you want to be an admin. ... I believe this was in March of 2011 at some point.

events.notes: Doc 208 is the docketed "corrected" 1/22/2015 transcript; original Doc 206 has same text at pp.119-120, Tr. 1149:12-1150:1.

events.text: Archive.org capture of silkroadmarket.org dated March 4, 2011 showed an open-web page directing users to the Tor Silk Road site.

cites.quote: So it captured this particular screen March 4, 2011, right? A. March 4, 2011, yes.

events.text: Testimony of Richard Bates: on March 15, 2011 Ulbricht left him a voicemail and then said in a Google chat that his site was down, possibly from too much traffic or his "amature coding."

cites.quote: My site is down and I don't know why. Too much traffic I think. I get an error about too many open connectons. Might be my amature coding

events.notes: GX 1005 (voicemail, ~6 pm Central) and GX 1006 (chat, 6:36 pm Central per Bates's time conversion). Doc 208 is the docketed "corrected" 1/22/2015 transcript; original Doc 206 has same text at p.100, Tr. 1130:2-21.

events.text: Email from staff@silkroadmarket.org to support@autovps.net (Karpeles-owned host) dated March 18, 2011 asked how to upgrade VPS memory; found in Karpeles Gmail search-warrant return.

cites.quote: It is from "staff@silkroadmarket.org." The date is March 18, 2011. It's to "support@autovps.net."

events.text: Laptop file 'Networthcalculator.ods' listed April 2011 with note 'launch sr'.

cites.quote: April 2011, net worth is listed here under that column as 29948, and the notes column says "launch sr," correct?

events.notes: File first saved 6/17/2012, last edited 12/2/2012 (Tr. 956:24-957:1).

events.text: Silk Road PGP key (name 'Silk Road', staff@silkroadmarket.org) was created April 1, 2011; private key file SilkRoad.asc found on defendant's laptop matched DPR's public key.

cites.quote: Q. What was the date this private key was created? A. April 1st, 2011.

events.notes: Also Der-Yeghiayan 200 Tr. 380:7-10 (key created April 1, 2011 at 4:47 a.m.).

events.text: Testimony of Richard Bates: in an April 1, 2011 Google chat, Bates (as an April Fool's joke) told Ulbricht he had told friends he knew who ran the site; Ulbricht urged him to be quieter.

cites.quote: All my friends think your site is really cool ... I told them I know the guy who runs it "Me: you should be quiter

events.notes: GX 1003. Doc 208 is the docketed "corrected" 1/22/2015 transcript; original Doc 206 has same text at pp.117-118, Tr. 1147:18-1148:1.

events.text: Defense established a June 2011 Gawker article about Silk Road after which site traffic increased significantly.
events.actors: HSI SA Jared Der-Yeghiayan; Joshua Dratel

cites.quote: In June 2011, there was an article on gawker.com about Silk Road, right? A. Yes, there was.

events.text: Testimony of Richard Bates: around June 2011, after a news report that Senator Chuck Schumer had asked the FBI to investigate, Bates told Ulbricht "they're looking for you," and Ulbricht answered "Yeah."
events.actors: Richard Bates; Ross Ulbricht; Sen. Charles Schumer

cites.quote: there was a news article about Chuck Schumer, you know, telling the FBI to investigate. I recall that being sometime in June of 2011.

events.notes: Bates said he continued providing programming help "into the summer of 2011" (Tr. 1130:7). Doc 208 is the docketed "corrected" 1/22/2015 transcript; original Doc 206 has same text at p.120, Tr. 1150:10-14.

events.text: HSI Chicago began monitoring unusual drug seizures at the O'Hare international mail branch linked to Silk Road (per HSI Chicago chronology in SA Der-Yeghiayan 3500 material).

cites.quote: -June of 2011, HSI Chicago started monitoring unusual drugs seizures from the Mail Branch related to the Silk Road
This is approximately June 2011. An officer brought to my attention several --

events.notes: Defense reply exhibit (ECF 232-6), an HSI Chicago internal chronology; author perspective is HSI Chicago.

events.text: First post by the Silk Road admin account on the new forum ('Business as usual'), announcing a separate forum server; signed 'Silk Road staff'.

cites.quote: We have it running on a separate server with its own URL so that if the main site ever goes down again, first check here for updates.
DPR's first posting to the forum was June 18, 2011. At that time DPR's username on the forum was simply "SilkRoad."

events.notes: DPR forum account registered around June 2011 (Tr. 245:5-7). Defense referenced June 5 / June 11, 2011 site-closure messages (202 Tr. 626:12; 200 Tr. 467:3-5). Also in evidence as GX 125A (Tr. 2112:21-22). Compare Alford's civil-forfeiture statement that Silk Road "in its current form" dates to about June 18, 2011 (Doc 214, Tr. 1406:24-1407:1).

events.text: DPR/Silk Road forum post announced a new 'forgeries' category for forged government-issued documents including fake IDs and passports.

cites.quote: we are happy to announce a new category in the marketplace called forgeries.

events.notes: GX 125H.

events.text: By stipulation, DEA SA Shelby Richardson made eight undercover purchase attempts on Silk Road between September 2011 and May 2013 as "downersforyou," from a computer in the Southern District of New York; every substance received tested positive for illegal drugs.
events.actors: DEA SA Shelby Richardson; DEA chemist Russell J. Gallis

cites.quote: from September 2011 to May 2013, Special Agent Richardson attempted a total of eight undercover purchases from the Silk Road website

events.notes: Range end 2013-05. GX 802/802A. The undercover account is spelled "downers4u" on the 2013 hacking-pack receipt (Doc 212, Tr. 1614:10).

events.text: About 3,600 drug-containing envelopes were seized at the O'Hare mail facility from October 2011 through April 2013.

cites.quote: This was from October 2011 through April 2013.

events.notes: Range end 2013-04.

events.text: Testimony of Richard Bates: in an October 6, 2011 TorChat, Bates asked Ulbricht ("myself") whether he had a job "besides the site," and Ulbricht said "nope"; Bates testified "the site" meant Silk Road.

cites.quote: So, here, on October 6, 2011, you say: "You don't have a job besides the site right now, do you?" And "myself" responds: "Nope."

events.notes: GX 228. Bates said he and Ulbricht worked on a bitcoin-exchange project that "ramped up around the September and October timeframe" (Tr. 1131:18-19) but also dated its start to "November of 2011" (Tr. 1132:10): internal inconsistency. Doc 208 is the docketed "corrected" 1/22/2015 transcript; original Doc 206 has same text at pp.124-125, Tr. 1154:22-1155:2.

events.text: Testimony of SA Gary Alford: an October 11, 2011 bitcointalk.org post by "Altoid," seeking an IT pro for a "venture backed bitcoin start-up," asked applicants to write to RossUlbricht@gmail.com; this linked Altoid to Ulbricht.

cites.quote: If interested, please, send your answer to the following questions to RossUlbricht@G mail.com.

events.notes: Defense cross stressed that the Altoid posts dated from 2011 and were findable by anyone using Google (Doc 214, Tr. 1397:20-1399:22).

events.text: HSI Chicago opened case "Operation Dime Store" to document Silk Road-linked mail seizures.

cites.quote: On October 13, 2011, HSI Chicago opened case Operation Dime Store to document the findings of the seizures coming into the mail branch.
Q. When was that? A. It was October 2011.

events.notes: He first heard of the site approx. late Sept/early Oct 2011 (Tr. 88:1). Bitcoin ~$2-4 then (198 Tr. 153:21-22).

events.text: Silk Road forum post titled 'site outage' dated Oct 19, 2011 (pictures not backed up).

cites.quote: This is dated October 19, 2011, the title is "site outage".
We're having to rebuild the site from a backup. ... The site just went live.

events.notes: Range end 2011-10-22. GX 125D/125E per the court and AUSA (Tr. 2115:5-10). The defense had raised the October 19, 2011 outage with Alford (Doc 214, Tr. 1412:13-1413:11).

events.text: Richard Bates testified that Ulbricht told him on November 11, 2011 that he had sold the Silk Road website.

cites.quote: Bates also testified that Ulbricht told Bates, November 11, 2011, that he had sold the Silk Road website.
And he told me that he couldn't shut down the site because he had already sold it to someone else.

events.notes: 2d Cir (App. 19a) says only "in November 2011"; Bates also cited a Feb 2013 Google chat ("not [his] problem anymore"). Compare Dec. 9, 2011 Tor chat (GX 226D) in which "myself" told vj two people "think I sold the site" (Tr. 1191:4-12). Doc 208 is the docketed "corrected" 1/22/2015 transcript; original Doc 206 has same text at p.128, Tr. 1158:4-20.

events.text: Photograph of a seized Netherlands envelope ('Candy Shop' ecstasy) at O'Hare taken Dec 4, 2011; Der-Yeghiayan matched it to Silk Road vendor Candy Shop listings.

cites.quote: This photo was taken December 4, 2011.

events.text: Government introduced a December 9, 2011 Tor chat in which Ulbricht told vj that two people knew of his involvement but believed he had sold the site.

cites.quote: Ulbricht responded: “[U]nfortunately yes. There are two, but they think I sold the site and got out and they are quite convinced of it.”
There are two, but they think I sold the site and got out and they are quite convinced of it.

events.notes: Offered to rebut the defense claim that Ulbricht had left Silk Road in 2011. Read by AUSA Howard after Bates's testimony; government links this to Bates and ex-girlfriend Julia (Tr. 1139:1-2). Doc 208 is the docketed "corrected" 1/22/2015 transcript; original Doc 206 has same text at p.181, Tr. 1211:4-12.

events.text: Der-Yeghiayan photographed a seized Netherlands LSD envelope beside his laptop logged into the matching Silk Road listing.

cites.quote: I took it on December 30th, 2011.

events.notes: GX 102B.

events.text: Defense established that as of Dec 30, 2011 Silk Road instituted a new bitcoin system.
events.actors: HSI SA Jared Der-Yeghiayan; Joshua Dratel

cites.quote: as of December 30, 2011, Silk Road instituted a new bitcoin system?

events.notes: Question by defense; refreshed recollection.

events.text: Complaint states that throughout 2012-2013 Force, as the lead undercover agent, communicated with DPR using the authorized persona "Nob," posing as a drug smuggler, while Bridges served as the Baltimore task force's computer-forensics expert.

cites.quote: FORCE was the lead undercover agent in communication with DPR, the owner, administrator and operator of the Silk Road website.| BRIDGES was the computer forensics expert

events.notes: Range end 2013. Complaint alleges Force withheld PGP private keys and many decrypted communications from the case file and prosecutor (p.14-15). OCR text (the .ocr.txt has no form-feeds; pinpoint is PDF page from per-page OCR); verify quote against PDF.

events.text: Around January 2012 Silk Road's lead administrator adopted the username Dread Pirate Roberts; DPR signed posts with a PGP key whose private key was later found on Ulbricht's laptop.

cites.quote: Around January 2012, the Silk Road user who represented himself as the lead administrator of the site adopted the username Dread Pirate Roberts.

events.notes: PGP key recovery: App. 15a.

events.text: Der-Yeghiayan's first undercover buys on Silk Road began approximately January 2012.

cites.quote: Q. Your first buys were when? A. I believe it was January 2012.

events.notes: He made 50+ undercover buys total (198 Tr. 176:8-9).

events.text: Silk Road commission structure changed in January 2012.
events.actors: HSI SA Jared Der-Yeghiayan; Joshua Dratel

cites.quote: January 2012 was when the commission structure changed, correct

events.notes: Defense question.

events.text: HSI Baltimore SA Gregory Miller opened a Silk Road investigation after a CI began giving details about Silk Road on 2011-12-29.

cites.quote: On January 03, 2012, HSI Baltimore SA Gregory Miller opened investigation BA13CR12BA0016

disputes.title: When Silk Road launched
disputes.text: The transaction database starts on Feb 6, 2011, and the clearnet domain was registered Feb 28, 2011. A 2013 HSI draft affidavit said March 2011. The civil forfeiture complaint SA Alford signed said the site 'in its current form' dates to June 18, 2011, and the defense leaned on that date.

disputes.title: How the FBI found the Iceland server
disputes.text: Tarbell's declaration says the real IP leaked through the login/CAPTCHA page in early June 2013. The defense's Horowitz declaration called that account implausible given the server configuration. The government said no contemporaneous records exist beyond a 19-line log excerpt, and disclosed that Iceland had imaged a different server ('Server-1') around June 6, 2013. The court never reached the merits, ruling Ulbricht lacked standing.

disputes.title: Server access in July vs. takedown in October
disputes.text: Iceland imaged the server on July 23, 2013 and the FBI had a copy by about July 29. The site kept running until Oct 2. The defense pressed this gap at trial.

disputes.title: When HSI confronted Ulbricht about the fake IDs
disputes.text: Testimony and the Second Circuit put the HSI visit on about July 26, 2013. The defense opening said 'that day in September.'

disputes.title: Pen/trap order dates
disputes.text: Tarbell gives Sept 17–20, 2013. The court's list starts with an order on Sept 16, and sources differ on the date of the second order.

disputes.title: Value of the laptop bitcoins
disputes.text: The 144,000 BTC on the laptop are valued at $16–18 million at arrest by the court and the government, and at $29 million at seizure in defense cross-examination.

disputes.title: The Flush-account theft: Jan 25 or 26, 2013?
disputes.text: Bridges' plea and the N.D. Cal. complaint say Jan 25. SDNY filings date DPR's report of the theft to Jan 26.

disputes.title: DeathFromAbove's $250,000 demand
disputes.text: The N.D. Cal. complaint dates the identity-and-demand message Apr 10, 2013. The SDNY's Feb 1, 2015 letter and the Second Circuit say Apr 16.

disputes.title: When SDNY knew, and what it disclosed
disputes.text: Court and government say the Force letter reached the defense Dec 1, 2014; the defense brief also says Dec 3. The government told the court Bridges became a target only after November 2014, but Bridges' plea shows FBI and OIG interviews on May 28 and Nov 13, 2014.

disputes.title: Sentencing date
disputes.text: The judgment and sentencing transcript give May 29, 2015. The docket minute entry says 'Sentencing held on 6/1/2015', the day the judgment was filed.

disputes.title: How many murders-for-hire
disputes.text: The district court counted six solicitations; the Second Circuit five, noting the Jan 2013 'Flush' solicitation was not presented at trial. A trial stipulation said Canada had no record of the named victims or of the homicides.

disputes.title: Secondary-source errors
disputes.text: Lacson & Jones (2016) describe the corrupt agents as 'FBI agents.' Force was DEA and Bridges was Secret Service.
